newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tchibo, KJS leave coffee prices same for now.
newsitem.headline: Tchibo, KJS leave coffee prices same for now.

text.p: German coffee roasters Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) and Tchibo Frisch-Roest-Kaffee GmbH will leave their retail prices of roasted coffee unchanged for now, spokesmen for the two companies said on Thursday.

But they also said they were watching the situation very closely after an announcement by competitor Eduscho GmbH & Co KG earlier today it would raise the price of one of its mild coffees by one mark to 7.99 marks per 0.5 kg on February 3.
They did not rule out price increases at a later stage, but would not give envisaged dates or sizes.
A Tchibo spokesman said the firm dollar and tight availability of premium coffees in the raw materials market, cited by Eduscho, were a market-wide phenomenon.
"Crop prospects show there will be no easing of the tightness in quality coffees...we also see the necessity of price increases, albeit not at this immediate stage," the Tchibo spokesman said.

Tchibo last month put its market share of roasted coffee volumes at 19 percent while Eduscho pegged its share at 11 percent and KJS, which is part of U.S. food group Philip Morris quoted an October figure of 30.7 percent.
The average price of Tchibo products was at around 8.00 marks per 0.5 kg, with the average German retail price 0.50-0.60 lower.
A KJS spokesman put the average price of its products at 6.92 marks in the first week of January.
"We're observing the situation but we're not planning a move at this very moment," he said.
Tchibo plans to buy Eduscho, which posted losses over the last two years, pending cartel authority approval.
